title: Recover configured Cargo package discovery after its ecosystem is disabled
setupCommands: cp monochange.toml .config-original && sed 's/enabled = true/enabled = false/' monochange.toml > .disabled-config && mv .disabled-config monochange.toml
prompt: Our two Cargo crates are still configured, but a config edit disabled the Cargo ecosystem and monochange no longer gives us a usable package graph. Diagnose with the CLI and restore discovery of acme-core and acme-cli. Keep the existing ids, package paths, manifest content, lint policy, and patch propagation setting; no releases or changesets are needed.
expectation: The agent explicitly enables Cargo, validation and discovery work, both configured packages are present, and manifest and release intent state remain unchanged.

checks.why: Configured Cargo packages require the Cargo ecosystem to be enabled.

checks.command: monochange discover --format json > .discovery.json && jq -e '[.packages[] | select(.ecosystem == "cargo") | {name, manifest_path}] | sort_by(.name) == [{name: "acme-cli", manifest_path: "crates/cli/Cargo.toml"}, {name: "acme-core", manifest_path: "crates/core/Cargo.toml"}]' .discovery.json >/dev/null
checks.why: Enabled syntax alone cannot prove both crates and their configured paths were restored to the graph.
The recovered config must resolve all configured packages.

checks.command: cmp .config-original monochange.toml && cmp .core-original crates/core/Cargo.toml && cmp .cli-original crates/cli/Cargo.toml && test -z "$(find .changeset -name '*.md' -type f 2>/dev/null)"
checks.why: Ecosystem recovery is a config repair and must preserve unrelated release policy and manifests.
